turns.content: A gas-tight vessel contains A, B, and C and yields only water and a hydrogen halide after explosion. Gases A and B have a 1:1 volume ratio, and their densities at the same conditions differ by a factor of 2.11. What oxidizing-gas pair is consistent with those constraints?
The total-volume ratio is (A+B):C=1:2.25. Use the relations established so far to identify C and choose a convenient mole basis, keeping any unresolved identities symbolic.
For that mole basis, write the balanced contributions from each oxidizing gas reacting with C to form only the stated products.
Sum the products and calculate the mass percentage of the hydrogen halide, using consistent rounded molar masses.
State the percentage and identify the product species used in that mass fraction.
Check the elemental balance in the proposed reactions and recompute the total product mass on the same mole basis.
Report the gas identities, reaction rationale, and final product mass fraction obtained from the analysis.
